analysis: The PR is documentation-only. docs/provider/cli-reference.md changes a "Last updated" date and the runtime-constants table (head lines ~1937-1940). That table now cites CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift for reconnect backoff. It adds a 60 s stable-session reset counted from the register frame, and a 0..1 s randomized reconnect wait after close code 1012 with no backoff growth. docs/provider/troubleshooting.md updates the same source reference and the date at line 140. No code, auth, attestation, encryption, key-handling or cache logic changes. I checked the changes against TB-002 (coordinator-provider WebSocket), T-010 and the availability-related threats. The documented reconnect behavior is operational: a short randomized delay after 1012 and backoff reset after 60 s of a stable session. The documentation does not describe or imply any weakening of attestation, grant or revocation. It does not touch T-053, whose re-registration must start a fresh socket nonce, proof and grant, or T-041 cache posture. Remaining unverified contract: the new constants (stableSessionDuration, serviceRestartDelayRange) are asserted from CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, which is not supplied. Whether the real code matches, and whether the 1012 fast reconnect has any load or abuse implication for the coordinator, belongs to a source-code review of that file. Because those docs are not security-sensitive, I raise no finding. The remaining cli-reference content in the supplied excerpt is unchanged context. The excerpt shows no security-relevant claims introduced by this PR.
